newsitem.title: USA: Army suspends top enlisted man on sex allegations.
newsitem.headline: Army suspends top enlisted man on sex allegations.

text.p: Army Chief of Staff Gen. Dennis Reimer on Monday suspended the service's top enlisted man from his duties pending resolution of allegations of sexual harassment made against him by a woman former soldier.

Reimer said that Sergeant Major of the Army Gene McKinney would be assigned to the Army's Military District of Washington, but would not serve as the senior enlisted adviser to Army leaders until the latest allegations in a growing Army sexual harassment scandal were settled.

Pressure has grown from some members of Congress for the Army to suspend McKinney after Brenda Hoster, a 22-year veteran who retired last year, charged this month that she rejected pressure from McKinney for sex in a hotel room in Hawaii last April.
McKinney has denied any wrongdoing in the case, but some Republican senators last week pressed Army Secretary Togo West to suspend him until the issue is settled.

The charges by Hoster were the latest allegation in a scandal which began last November when male trainers at the Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland were charged with harassing and even raping young female recruits.
Similar charges have since emerged at other bases.
